note: Instance-level rubrics for the jaq interface-segregation case. Each criterion is answerable from the natural task prompt, the solver's patch, the repository, and the checker output without reproducing any particular reference repair. Any sound interface split that preserves behavior satisfies them.

rubrics.criterion: The trait that the jaq-core crate offers as the universal value contract no longer requires the string/number/sequence capability methods (such as sequence conversion, integer testing, machine-size and floating-point number access, UTF-8 string interpretation, byte access, string shortening, and byte-to-UTF-8 construction) of every implementor; those capabilities are reachable to the callers that need them through a focused interface implemented only by value types that actually have the capabilities.
rubrics.rationale: This is the load-bearing resolution of the merged-contract regression named first in the task prompt: a value type supporting only core filters is still forced to provide the full standard-library capability surface unless the fat contract is split.

rubrics.criterion: The data-kind contract in jaq-core no longer blankets every data kind with the input-stream capability: providing input-stream access (the inputs consumed by the `inputs`/`input` filters) is opt-in for a data kind, and kinds built purely from a lookup table are not required to provide anything input-related.
rubrics.rationale: The second regression named in the prompt is the mandatory input capability on the run-time data contract; the resolution is judged on the ownership of the requirement, not on the mechanics of any single crate layout.

rubrics.criterion: The standard-library filters that consume the value capabilities and the input stream obtain them by declaring the narrower interfaces they actually rely on (for example through bounded generics over the data or value type), so a caller that lacks a capability can no longer satisfy the filter signatures by way of a widened universal contract.
rubrics.rationale: Splitting traits without re-pointing their consumers would leave the merged surface load-bearing; the repair is complete only when the capability demand flows through the new focused interfaces at the filter signatures.

rubrics.criterion: The JSON value implementation in jaq-json satisfies each interface it actually supports: the capability methods retain their behavior under the reorganized trait structure (the same concrete value type keeps supporting string/number/sequence operations), and no leftover implementation items, orphaned impl blocks, or re-export aliases of a merged trait remain from the unification.
rubrics.rationale: The only in-tree value implementor must carry the workload through the reorganization; stranded impl items would silently narrow its capabilities while keeping the tree compiling.

rubrics.criterion: The standard-library layer once again defines its own extension surface for the value type rather than aliasing the core contract, and the convenience helpers built on the capability methods live with the interface and callers that use them, without duplicated helper bodies.
rubrics.rationale: The alias was the compatibility disguise that made the merge invisible; the layer separation the prompt asks for needs a distinct standard-library interface rather than a renamed pointer to the merged one.

rubrics.criterion: No degenerate compliance implementation remains whose only purpose is to satisfy a widened bound: in particular no always-empty input-stream stub (leaked allocation or otherwise) and no unimplemented or panicking default method that stands in for a real capability.
rubrics.rationale: The empty-stream leak and its conceptual equivalents are the observable residue of the mandatory capability; keeping any such shim means the payment the prompt complains about is still being made.

rubrics.criterion: No dead helper methods, unused convenience wrappers, or capability methods with empty default bodies remain in the core value contract after the split, and imports that previously resolved only through the unification do not leave unused-import warnings behind in workspace crates.
rubrics.rationale: The unification deliberately folded one trait away and deleted its helper; a repair that strands those leftovers in the core contract re-implements the same dead-weight smell at a smaller scale.

rubrics.criterion: Observable value behavior is not degraded for end users of the standard library: string operations (interpolation, length, splitting, trimming, explode/implode, slicing at byte offsets, UTF-8 validation) and numeric behavior (integer recognition, integer-size access, floating-point conversion including out-of-range rounding) produce the same results as before for the same filters and inputs.
rubrics.rationale: The capability split moves requirements between traits; a resolution that loses or rewires the actual byte/number operations behind the moved signatures would trade an interface defect for a behavior defect.

rubrics.criterion: The input-stream capability plumbing does not become universal-by-fallback: applications that construct a data kind without an input stream do not become quietly runnable into `inputs`/`input` yielding empty streams; absence of the capability is expressed in the type structure, not simulated at run time.
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific: the empty-stream stand-in is precisely the kind of sentinel that converts a design constraint into silent wrong behavior for embedders; preserving the opt-in capability means compilation, not a run-time no-op, decides whether inputs can be read.

rubrics.criterion: jaq-core remains a no_std-friendly crate: the reorganized contracts and the code that carries the input-stream or value-capability machinery inside the core crate do not introduce dependencies on standard-library-only APIs that previously lived in higher layers.
rubrics.rationale: The machinery was deliberately no_std-clean before it moved; a repair that drags standard-only APIs into core while splitting interfaces would break the feature combinations the workspace ships.
